title: Machine Learning
reference_explanation: Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence where algorithms learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed for every rule.

title: Cloud Computing
reference_explanation: Cloud computing delivers computing resources such as servers, storage, databases and software over the internet on demand, allowing scalable pay-as-you-go access.

title: Artificial Intelligence
reference_explanation: Artificial intelligence enables computer systems to perform tasks associated with human intelligence, including learning, reasoning, perception and language understanding.

title: Cyber Security
reference_explanation: Cyber security protects computer systems, networks, programs and data from unauthorized access, attack, damage or disruption using people, processes and technology.

title: Blockchain
reference_explanation: Blockchain is a distributed digital ledger that records transactions in linked, tamper-resistant blocks validated by a network of participants.

title: Internet of Things
reference_explanation: The Internet of Things connects physical devices with sensors and software to the internet so they can collect, exchange and act on data.

title: Data Science
reference_explanation: Data science combines statistics, programming and domain knowledge to collect, analyze and communicate insights from structured and unstructured data.

title: Operating Systems
reference_explanation: An operating system manages computer hardware and software resources, provides services for programs, and acts as an interface between users and the machine.

title: Computer Networks
reference_explanation: A computer network connects devices so they can communicate and share data and resources through protocols and transmission media.

title: DBMS
reference_explanation: A database management system is software that creates, stores, organizes, retrieves and controls access to structured data in databases.
